properties.LongDescription:
Formally occupied and owned by a rail company who have utilised it for their depot and residential training centre over the years now offer it for sale as a whole. The site is located close to and just off junction 12 of the M1 motorway and is about 7.5 acres in total offering:

• Transport yard of about 25,000 Sq. Ft.
• Workshop and office complex of about 1,800 Sq. ft. GIA
• 6 bedroom, 4 reception room farmhouse with exposed beams. Inglenook fireplaces, gallery landing, en-suites and farmhouse kitchen
• Annex (currently used commercially)
• Further transport/storage area of about 25,000 Sq. Ft
• 1.3 acres of ancillary outside storage area
• 5,800 Sq. Ft tarmacked car park with 16 spaces
• About 4.2 acres of ancillary land with stream (currently overgrown)

Beyond the car park, accessible on the other side of a stream, is about 4.2 acres of what we have described as ancillary land. Believed to be level, but currently overgrown and redundant in use.

All in all, the site presents many opportunities as either an investment by way of separating the elements and letting them separately, or by owner occupation, or a combination of both living in the property, using some and letting some of the elements. Alternatively, subject to the grant of planning, there could be potential to develop parts to add more industrial units and create a small industrial park.

The farmhouse sits in the middle of the site with the annex, workshop and office complex to one side. To the other is a further transport and storage area along with the training/office buildings. (excluded from the sale). Behind is a raised area of about 1.3 Acres offering further open air storage and to the front sits the carpark, and transport depot.  Beyond the car park accessible on the other side of a stream is about 4.2 Acres of what we have described as ancillary land.

Believed to be level, but currently overgrown and redundant in use.  All in all the site presents many opportunities as either an investment by way of separating the elements and letting them separately, or by owner occupation, or a combination of both living in the property, using some and letting some of the elements. Description

A rare opportunity to acquire an exceptional building plot with full planning permission granted for a striking contemporary country residence, set within a historic walled garden in the heart of the Hertfordshire countryside. The Walled Garden is positioned within a registered Grade II Listed Park & Garden, adjoining a distinguished Grade II* Listed Building, occupying a truly special setting on the edge of the desirable village of Preston.

Surrounded by mature landscape and open countryside, the site offers privacy, heritage and architectural potential rarely found in such a location. The main residence has been designed to provide generous and flexible living accommodation, including expansive kitchen, dining and family areas, elegant reception spaces and a dedicated study, all arranged to maximise natural light and views across the surrounding countryside.

Complementing the principal house is a dedicated leisure pavilion, offering an impressive suite of lifestyle amenities including an indoor swimming pool, gymnasium, yoga studio, private cinema and wellness spaces, together with substantial underground garaging suitable for a luxury car collection. The approved scheme includes capacity for up to 16 vehicles, creating an exceptional facility for collectors or enthusiasts.

Planning

Planning permission was granted in March 2025 for the construction of a spectacular contemporary residence extending to approximately 16,500 sq ft, designed to deliver an exceptional standard of modern country living. The approved design incorporates a beautifully conceived six-bedroom home arranged across two interconnected elements, blending refined family living with private leisure and wellness facilities.

Sustainability has also been central to the design approach, with the proposed home designed to align with the principles of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) 2030 Climate Challenge. The scheme incorporates ultra-low energy technologies including photovoltaic solar panels and ground source heat pumps, alongside a carefully curated palette of sustainable materials such as charred timber cladding, handcrafted brickwork and a biodiverse green roof designed to enhance the surrounding landscape and encourage wildlife.

Development Opportunity

Importantly, while the approved scheme allows for a residence of approximately 16,500 sq ft with six bedrooms, the design has been conceived with flexibility in mind and can be readily tailored to suit a purchaser’s requirements. This could allow for a more modest yet equally impressive home of approximately 6,000–6,500 sq ft with three to four bedrooms, if preferred, enabling buyers to create a residence perfectly suited to their lifestyle while retaining the architectural integrity of the consented scheme.

Opportunities to create a new private residence within the grounds of a historic registered park and garden are exceptionally rare, particularly where a sensitively designed contemporary scheme has already secured full planning consent. The Walled Garden therefore represents a unique chance to deliver a landmark country home within an established heritage landscape — a setting that would be extremely difficult to replicate or secure through new planning today.
.
Extensive consultation with planning authorities, conservation specialists and heritage advisors has ensured that the proposal responds sensitively to its historic surroundings while delivering a bold and contemporary architectural statement.

The result is a rare opportunity to create a truly exceptional country home within a historic parkland setting, combining architectural quality, sustainability and lifestyle in one of Hertfordshire’s most desirable village locations.

Latest drawings for the GF-only scheme (Ground Floor) without the massive basement dig, also attached as an alternative option.

Detached 4-bed detached period house in the very popular village of Leckford in the Test Valley district of Hampshire.

Guide £600,000 - £650,000

For sale by online auction 18th December with bidding closing at 1pm

This is a lovely family home, with an inviting driveway for up to ten vehicles with the photo deck speaking for itself.

From the front door you will be welcomed by a hall that directs you to an open plan kitchen with integrated white goods, a double electric range cooker and larder, as well as a boot room, WC and utility, area, a delightful open plan dining area with feature window and office all laid with antico flooring with the dining area providing access via French Doors to a spacious garden area with decking which you will see from the photographs is quite outstanding, laid to lawn with a fishpond and larger than typical for the area, with rear gated access and well fenced.

Upstairs you will enjoy three double bedrooms, one with ensuite, a family bathroom with freestanding bath and a nice sized single all nicely carpeted giving a homely feel.
The location of this property is a real feature with access from the left to the village which includes three wonderful pubs, The Greyhound, Three Cups and The White Hart along with The Grosvenor Hotel as well as a plethora of independent shops including a butchers, café, a fruit and veg shop and the infamous ‘George Clarke’ Interior design boutique.

To the right of the property, you will enjoy the most magnificent country walks leading to Peats Spade, the Mayfly and then on to the ever-popular Leckford Estate, owned by The John Lewis Partnership with its delightful vineyard, nursery and Café.

Location and Travel:

Andover train station is around 15 minutes’ drive and provides train services to London Waterloo, Reading and Yeovil.

The historic City of Winchester is around q0 miles away and Salisbury with its 13th-century Gothic cathedral, its proximity to Stonehenge and its ancients roots a popular leisure visit over a weekend.

The accommodation is arranged as three separate units. To the front of the property is a one-bedroom flat, which has been converted and renovated within the last few years, providing modern and well-presented living space.
Accessed via the rear garden are two further properties. The first is a three-bedroom house, comprising a lounge/kitchen area on the ground floor along with a downstairs bathroom, and three bedrooms on the first floor. The second is a two-bedroom house, also featuring a lounge/kitchen on the ground floor, with two bedrooms and a family bathroom upstairs.
All three units are currently tenanted, ensuring a ready-made investment with established income from day one. The layout and configuration offer flexibility and strong ongoing rental demand, making this an excellent opportunity for both new and experienced landlords.
Situated in a central location within Thetford, the property benefits from convenient access to local amenities, transport links, and the town centre.

You are also within walking distance of a huge range of pubs, restaurants, and coffee shops .

The property needs modernisation and that the lease has 73 years remaining.

You may wish to extend the lease, and this will likely increase the value to £185,000 reflecting the current market.

To extend a lease in the UK, a leaseholder must formally serve a Section 42 notice on the landlord, typically their freeholder, this legally mandated process grants a 90-year extension and a zero-ground rent. Further advice can be gained from and this suggests the approximate cost to extend the lease would be approximately £17,000 plus legal costs.

Generally, you would need to have owned the flat for two years to extend a lease, however the owner of the flat is prepared to assign the benefit of having owned the flat for many years so the process of extending the lease would not be delayed.

The ground rent is currently £100 a year and the service charge is £1400 per year.
